questions.stem: A 63-year-old lady presents to the emergency department with sudden onset painful diminution of vision in the left eye. The symptoms began while she was watching a movie in a theatre. On examination, her left eye was congested, with a hazy cornea, shallow anterior chamber and mid-dilated, fixed pupil. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Acute angle closure glaucoma 

 

The patient's symptoms strongly suggest acute angle-closure glaucoma (AACG). Sudden, painful diminution of vision, redness (congestion), a hazy cornea, and a mid-dilated, fixed pupil are hallmark signs of AACG. The shallow anterior chamber adds further evidence, as this is a key predisposing factor for angle-closure glaucoma. The condition typically occurs in predisposed individuals when the pupil dilates (e.g., in a dim environment such as a theatre), causing the peripheral iris to obstruct aqueous outflow through the trabecular meshwork, leading to a rapid rise in intraocular pressure (IOP).

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Primary open-angle glaucoma: Primary open-angle glaucoma is generally asymptomatic in its early stages. It causes a gradual loss of vision over time without acute pain or redness. Other signs, such as frequent changes in presbyopic glasses or difficulty with dark adaptation, are absent in this case.

 

Option B. Acute conjunctivitis: Acute conjunctivitis often presents with redness and discharge but does not cause pain, a fixed pupil, or corneal haze. It is also not associated with acute diminution of vision.

 

Option D. Acute anterior uveitis: Acute anterior uveitis can cause pain and photophobia, but it does not usually present with a mid-dilated, fixed pupil or shallow anterior chamber. Furthermore, corneal haze is not a typical feature of uveitis.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Acute angle-closure glaucoma is characterized by sudden, painful loss of vision with redness, corneal haze, a shallow anterior chamber, and a mid-dilated, fixed pupil. It is a true ophthalmic emergency requiring immediate treatment to lower intraocular pressure.

questions.stem: You can use a stenopaeic slit for all of the following except:

options.label: D
options.text: To find out the axis in astigmatism

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Corneal tattooing.

 

A stenopaeic slit is a narrow slit used in ophthalmology to isolate light entering the eye in a particular meridian. It has several applications but is not used for corneal tattooing, which involves the application of dye to the cornea for cosmetic or therapeutic purposes in cases of blindness or corneal scarring.

 

Applications of stenopaeic slit:

 

  1. Fincham's test: Used to differentiate between lenticular and corneal opacities in cases of halos.
  2. Optical iridectomy: Helps identify the best meridian of vision in cases of optical defects caused by the iris.
  3. Astigmatism: Used to determine the axis of astigmatism by isolating the meridian with the clearest vision.

 

Corneal tattooing involves the use of India ink dye or similar pigments to blacken the cornea, which is purely cosmetic and does not require the use of a stenopaeic slit.

 

Educational Objective:

 

A stenopaeic slit is a diagnostic tool used for identifying optical defects, meridians in astigmatism, and differentiating pathologies but is not used for corneal tattooing, which is a cosmetic procedure involving the application of dye to a blind eye.

questions.stem: Schwalbe’s line corresponds to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Descemets membrane

 

Schwalbe’s line is a prominent anatomical landmark in the anterior segment of the eye, marking the termination of the Descemet's membrane at the corneal periphery. It represents the junction between the cornea and the trabecular meshwork, which is part of the drainage angle of the eye. This line is essential for identifying the boundaries of the anterior chamber angle during gonioscopy.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Corneal endothelium: Incorrect. The corneal endothelium is a thin monolayer of cells lining the inner surface of the cornea, but Schwalbe’s line specifically corresponds to the termination of Descemet's membrane, not the endothelium.

 

Option C. Schlemm’s canal: Incorrect. Schlemm’s canal is a circular channel in the eye that collects aqueous humor from the trabecular meshwork, but it is located deeper and does not correspond to Schwalbe’s line.

 

Option D. Ciliary body: Incorrect. The ciliary body is part of the uveal tract and is involved in aqueous humor production and accommodation. It is not anatomically related to Schwalbe’s line.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Schwalbe’s line is the anatomical landmark that corresponds to the termination of Descemet's membrane in the eye.

questions.stem: Ptosis occurs due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Oculomotor palsy

 

Ptosis refers to drooping of the upper eyelid and occurs due to weakness or paralysis of the levator palpebrae superioris muscle, which is innervated by the oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III). In cases of oculomotor palsy, the eyelid droops significantly, and other associated features include:

 

  • Eye being "down and out" due to unopposed action of the lateral rectus and superior oblique muscles.
  • Diplopia and pupil dilation may also occur, depending on the extent of nerve involvement.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Facial nerve palsy: Facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) palsy causes lagophthalmos (inability to close the eyelid) and not ptosis, as it affects the orbicularis oculi muscle.

 

Option C. Trigeminal palsy: Trigeminal nerve (cranial nerve V) palsy affects sensation in the face and cornea but does not cause ptosis.

 

Option D. Trochlear palsy: Trochlear nerve (cranial nerve IV) palsy affects the superior oblique muscle, leading to vertical diplopia but not ptosis.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Ptosis occurs due to oculomotor nerve palsy, as it innervates the levator palpebrae superioris muscle, responsible for elevating the upper eyelid.

questions.stem: A 38 year old female patient presents with loss of vision in both eyes. On examination normal pupillary responses are seen with normal fundus. VER shows extinguished response. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Cortical blindness

 

The key features in this case are loss of vision, normal pupillary responses, normal fundus, and an extinguished VER, which are diagnostic of cortical blindness. Cortical blindness results from bilateral damage to the occipital cortex, often caused by:

 

  • Ischemic stroke
  • Traumatic brain injury
  • Hypoxia
  • Infections or tumors affecting the occipital lobe.

 

The Visual Evoked Response (VER) is extinguished because the problem lies in the visual cortex, not in the eyes or optic nerves. Normal pupillary responses and fundus findings indicate that the afferent visual pathways up to the retina and optic nerve are intact.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Retrobulbar neuritis: Retrobulbar neuritis presents with loss of vision and often a normal fundus, but VER would not be extinguished, and there would be a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD).

 

Option C. Retinal detachment: Retinal detachment causes an abnormal fundus, showing detachment of the retina. It also does not cause extinguished VER as the visual cortex remains functional.

 

Option D. Hysteria: Hysteria (functional vision loss) involves subjective vision loss without any objective findings, and VER would be normal.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Cortical blindness is characterized by bilateral visual loss, normal fundus and pupillary responses, and an extinguished Visual Evoked Response (VER) due to occipital lobe dysfunction.

questions.stem: Which orbital wall is the strongest?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Lateral 

 

The lateral orbital wall is the strongest among the orbital walls. It is primarily composed of two robust bones: the zygomatic bone and the greater wing of the sphenoid bone. These bones provide significant structural support to the lateral aspect of the orbit, making it more resistant to trauma compared to the other orbital walls.

 

The strength of the lateral wall is essential because it serves as a barrier to protect the eye and orbital contents from lateral forces and impacts.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Medial: The medial orbital wall is thin and delicate, largely formed by the lacrimal bone and the ethmoid bone. Its thinness makes it more susceptible to fractures, such as in blowout injuries.

 

Option B. Inferior: The inferior orbital wall, formed by the maxillary bone and partly by the zygomatic bone, is relatively thin compared to the lateral wall. It is a common site for fractures in orbital trauma.

 

Option D. Superior: The superior orbital wall is formed by the frontal bone and the lesser wing of the sphenoid. While it is stronger than the medial and inferior walls, it is not as robust as the lateral wall.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The lateral orbital wall, composed of the zygomatic bone and the greater wing of the sphenoid, is the strongest orbital wall, providing critical protection to the orbit against lateral trauma.

questions.stem: A patient with history of running nose and pain over medial aspect of the eye presents with sudden onset of high grade fever, prostration, chemosis, proptosis and diplopia on lateral gaze with congestion of the optic disc. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans C) Cavernous sinus Thrombosis

 

The clinical presentation of cavernous sinus thrombosis includes:

 

  • A history of infection (e.g., sinusitis or facial infection).
  • Sudden onset of high-grade fever, prostration, and systemic signs of infection.
  • Pain and swelling in the medial aspect of the eye due to venous congestion.
  • Proptosis, chemosis, and diplopia (on lateral gaze) caused by cranial nerve involvement (III, IV, and VI).
  • Congestion of the optic disc due to impaired venous drainage.

 

Cavernous sinus thrombosis results from septic thrombus formation in the cavernous sinus, often due to the spread of infection from the face or paranasal sinuses via valveless veins. It is a medical emergency requiring urgent treatment with intravenous antibiotics and, in some cases, anticoagulation or surgical drainage.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Acute ethmoidal sinusitis: Incorrect; while ethmoidal sinusitis can cause pain over the medial aspect of the eye, it does not explain the systemic symptoms (fever, prostration) or orbital signs like proptosis and chemosis.

 

Option B. Orbital cellulitis: Incorrect; orbital cellulitis presents with fever, proptosis, and chemosis but typically lacks diplopia on lateral gaze caused by cranial nerve involvement or optic disc congestion.

 

Option D. Orbital apex syndrome: Incorrect; orbital apex syndrome involves cranial nerves II, III, IV, and VI and causes optic nerve dysfunction (vision loss) but does not usually cause systemic signs like high fever or prostration.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Cavernous sinus thrombosis is characterized by sudden-onset systemic infection signs (fever, prostration) along with chemosis, proptosis, optic disc congestion, and diplopia due to cranial nerve involvement, often following sinusitis or facial infection.

questions.stem: During a lecture on vector-borne diseases, the topic shifts to the landmark discoveries that shaped our understanding of malaria transmission. Which of the following scientists is credited with uncovering the role of Anopheline mosquitoes in the transmission of malaria?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Ronald Ross

 

Sir Ronald Ross is credited with the discovery that Anopheline mosquitoes play a key role in the transmission of malaria. In 1897, while working in India, Ross demonstrated the life cycle of the malaria parasite, specifically identifying how it is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected Anopheline mosquito. His groundbreaking work laid the foundation for the control and prevention of malaria, which ultimately led to his Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1902.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Laveran: Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran discovered the malaria parasite, Plasmodium, in 1880. However, he did not identify the role of mosquitoes in malaria transmission. His discovery was a crucial step in understanding malaria as a parasitic disease, but he did not establish the vector-borne aspect of transmission.

 

Option C. Muller: Paul Hermann Müller was awarded the Nobel Prize for his discovery of the insecticidal properties of DDT, which became instrumental in malaria control. However, he did not contribute directly to the understanding of malaria transmission by mosquitoes.

 

Option D. Pampana: Giovanni Battista Grassi and his colleagues made significant contributions to understanding malaria transmission, but "Pampana" is not an actual figure associated with malaria research. It is likely a fictional name included by examiners.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Ronald Ross is the scientist credited with discovering the role of Anopheline mosquitoes in malaria transmission, a key finding in the fight against malaria.

questions.stem: Using goggles while driving a bike is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Primary prevention

 

Using goggles while driving a bike falls under primary prevention. Primary prevention aims to reduce the risk of developing injury or disease by providing specific protection against potential hazards. In this case, goggles protect the eyes from foreign bodies, dust, or insects that could cause eye injury while riding a bike. Using goggles while driving a bike is an example of primary prevention because it provides specific protection against potential eye injuries from foreign bodies, dust, or debris.

Ans. B) Thin smear with Acridine orange stain

 

The Thin smear with Acridine orange stain is recognized for having extremely high sensitivity and specificity, often reported to be close to 100% in detecting malaria parasites. Acridine orange is a fluorescent dye that binds to nucleic acids and allows rapid visualization of the parasites under a fluorescence microscope. The primary advantage of this method is the speed, as results can be obtained within 3 to 10 minutes, significantly faster compared to traditional staining methods. This rapid detection is crucial in clinical settings where timely diagnosis can be life-saving.

questions.stemHtml: A study is investigating the multifactorial causes of lung cancer, including known and unknown contributing factors. Which of the following models of disease causation is depicted in the image below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Rothman’s sufficient cause model

 

Rothman’s sufficient cause model, also known as the "causal pie model," describes how multiple component causes come together to result in the occurrence of a disease. According to this model, a disease can result when a "sufficient cause" is completed, which is made up of a combination of individual "component causes." These component causes can vary between different individuals or populations but generally include both necessary and contributing factors.

 

To understand this, imagine the model as a set of pies, with each pie representing a complete causal mechanism for a disease. Each slice of a pie represents a component cause. Some components are unique to certain pies, while others may appear in multiple pies. Importantly, at least one factor, termed the "necessary cause," must be present in all pies for the disease to occur. For example, in the context of tuberculosis, exposure to Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a necessary cause, while factors like malnutrition, overcrowding, or HIV infection act as component causes.

 

Rothman, an epidemiologist, proposed this model to explain the complex interplay between different risk factors and how they collectively lead to disease.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Bradford Hill criteria: The Bradford Hill criteria outline a set of principles used to establish a causal relationship between a specific factor and a disease. The most crucial criterion is "temporality," meaning that the cause must precede the effect. These criteria are widely used in epidemiological studies but do not address the multifactorial nature of disease causation in the way that Rothman's model does.

 

Option C. Dahlgren-Whitehead model: The Dahlgren-Whitehead model is a socio-ecological model that explains the layers of influence on individual health. It emphasizes how factors like individual behavior, social and community networks, and general socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental conditions contribute to health inequalities. It does not focus on the necessary and component causes of disease as Rothman’s model does.

 

Option D. Life course approach: The life course approach studies how social, environmental, and biological factors throughout an individual’s life affect health outcomes. It incorporates various life stages and considers how early life experiences influence health in later years. While it recognizes the multifactorial nature of disease, it is more focused on how cumulative exposure over time impacts health rather than outlining a specific model of disease causation.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Rothman’s sufficient cause model emphasizes the concept of necessary and component causes working together to form a sufficient cause for disease. Recognize that a necessary cause must always be present, while other contributing factors (component causes) complete the causal mechanism.

options.label: A
options.text: Its residual action is similar to DDT

options.label: B
options.text: It is derived from vegetable sources

options.label: C
options.text: It functions primarily as a contact poison

options.label: D
options.text: It shows synergistic effects when combined with DDT

questions.answerText: Its residual action is similar to DDT
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Its residual action is similar to DDT

 

Pyrethrum is a natural insecticide derived from the chrysanthemum plant. It has specific properties that make it effective as an insecticide but also set it apart from synthetic agents like DDT. One of the key differences between Pyrethrum and DDT is their residual action. Pyrethrum breaks down rapidly when exposed to light, air, and moisture, giving it virtually no residual effect. In contrast, DDT is known for its long-lasting residual action, which can persist for several months on surfaces. Thus, the statement "Its residual action is similar to DDT" is incorrect because Pyrethrum's effectiveness diminishes quickly, whereas DDT's effect can last for an extended period.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. It is derived from vegetable sources: This statement is true. Pyrethrum is indeed derived from the dried flower heads of the chrysanthemum plant. It is a natural insecticide extracted from a botanical source.

 

Option C. It functions primarily as a contact poison: This statement is also correct. Pyrethrum works mainly as a contact insecticide, targeting the nervous system of insects and causing paralysis. It disrupts the normal function of nerve cells by altering sodium channel activity, leading to nerve damage.

 

Option D. It shows synergistic effects when combined with DDT: This statement is accurate. Pyrethrum can be combined with DDT or other chemicals to enhance the insecticidal effect, demonstrating a synergistic action. The combination often increases the overall effectiveness of pest control treatments.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Differences between Pyrethrum and synthetic insecticides, particularly in terms of residual action. Pyrethrum has almost no residual action compared to DDT, which can persist for extended periods. Additionally, recognize that Pyrethrum is a natural insecticide that functions as a contact poison and can act synergistically with other agents.

questions.stem: In evaluating public health strategies, a health department aims to assess the overall burden of diseases and the success of respective interventions. Which index is best suited for this purpose?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Disability Adjusted Life Years 

 

The Disability Adjusted Life Year (DALY) is a comprehensive measure that combines both the years lost due to premature death and the years lived with disability. This metric provides a holistic view of the burden of diseases by accounting for the impact of both mortality and morbidity. By combining these factors, DALYs allow public health authorities to measure the total health loss and evaluate the effectiveness of interventions aimed at reducing disease burden. Specifically, DALYs quantify the "years of healthy life" lost, which can reflect the success or limitations of health programs in alleviating this burden.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Case fatality rate: This metric represents the proportion of individuals who die from a specific disease among those diagnosed with it. While useful in assessing the lethality or "virulence" of a disease, it does not account for the total disease burden as it focuses only on mortality and excludes factors like disability.

 

Option C. Dependency ratio: This index indicates the proportion of dependents (individuals typically younger than 15 or older than 64) to the working-age population. It is mainly used to assess the economic burden on the working population, rather than the health burden associated with diseases or disabilities.

 

Option D. Prevalence of the disease: This represents the total number of cases of a disease within a population at a given time. While it provides insights into the spread of disease, it does not capture the severity or the combined impact of mortality and morbidity.

 

Educational Objective:

questions.stem: As per The Prudent Diet by WHO the maximum recommended dietary intake of cholesterol per day is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) 200 mg/day


The World Health Organization (WHO) developed the Prudent Diet as a dietary guideline to prevent coronary heart disease (CHD). One of the key recommendations of this diet is to limit cholesterol intake to a maximum of 200 mg per day. This helps to reduce the risk of elevated blood cholesterol levels, which are associated with an increased risk of CHD. Cholesterol levels in the blood can be influenced by dietary cholesterol, and limiting intake helps maintain healthier lipid profiles.

 

The Prudent Diet emphasizes a total cholesterol to HDL (high-density lipoprotein) ratio of less than 3.5, achieved through dietary modifications, such as reducing fat intake (specifically saturated fats) and salt, while increasing complex carbohydrates and avoiding alcohol. These recommendations collectively help in maintaining lower cholesterol levels and promoting cardiovascular health.

 

Educational Objective:


The maximum recommended dietary intake of cholesterol per day, according to WHO’s Prudent Diet, is 200 mg.

 

Remember:

 

The Prudent Diet by WHO – Key Recommendations

 

  1. Goal: Maintain a cholesterol to HDL ratio of less than 3.5 to reduce the risk of coronary heart disease.
  2. Fat Intake: Limit total fat intake to less than 30% of daily calories.
  3. Saturated Fat: Keep saturated fat intake below 7% of total calories.
  4. Salt Intake: Restrict salt intake to less than 5 grams per day.
  5. Total Cholesterol Intake: Ensure total cholesterol intake is below 200 mg per day.
  6. Complex Carbohydrates: Increase intake of complex carbohydrates to improve overall dietary balance.
  7. Alcohol: Avoid alcohol to support heart health.

questions.stemHtml: What is the name of this syringe technology discovered by Marc Koska?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) K1 auto-disable syringe

 

Marc Koska invented the K1 auto-disable syringe, also known as a "solo-shot" or "single-shot" syringe. This syringe technology is significant because it is specifically designed to prevent reuse. The K1 auto-disable syringe operates by breaking the plunger mechanism after a single use. Once the vaccine or medication is administered and the plunger is fully depressed, the syringe becomes unusable, effectively preventing any further use. This feature is crucial in reducing the risk of transmitting blood-borne infections (BBIs) such as HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C, which can occur through the reuse of contaminated syringes.

 

The K1 auto-disable syringe is particularly important in public health programs, such as the Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) program, where it is used to ensure safe and efficient immunization. It was also widely utilized during COVID-19 vaccination efforts in India, emphasizing its role in maintaining safety standards during mass immunization campaigns.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Safety-Lok syringe: This is incorrect. Safety-Lok syringes are equipped with a locking mechanism to prevent needlestick injuries but do not have the auto-disable feature that stops syringe reuse.

 

Option B. Vanish Point syringe: This option is also incorrect. Vanish Point syringes are retractable syringes that automatically retract the needle into the barrel after the injection, minimizing needlestick injuries but not specifically preventing reuse like the K1 auto-disable syringe.

 

Option D. Monoject syringe: This is incorrect as well. Monoject syringes are standard disposable syringes used for various medical applications, without the auto-disable feature specifically designed to prevent reuse.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The importance and mechanism of the K1 auto-disable syringe, which was invented by Marc Koska. The key concept is that the syringe is designed to become nonfunctional after one use, preventing the risk of transmitting blood-borne infections (HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C, Malaria, Syphilis). This technology is vital in public health immunization programs to ensure safety and avoid the spread of diseases through reused syringes.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Obese and Non-obese persons

 

In a case-control study, two groups are chosen based on the outcome (the presence or absence of a disease), not the exposure. Here, the objective is to explore the link between ordering food online (exposure) and obesity (outcome). Thus, the study needs a "case" group with obesity and a "control" group without obesity. By comparing these two groups, the intern can look back to see the history of online food ordering in both groups and determine any association between online food ordering and obesity.

 

In this setup:

 

  • Cases are individuals with obesity.
  • Controls are individuals without obesity.

 

Using these groups allows the researcher to observe whether there is a statistically significant relationship between ordering food online and developing obesity.

 

Other Options

 

Option A. Only Obese persons: If only obese individuals are selected, there would be no comparison group without obesity, which is essential in a case-control study. This setup would not allow for an evaluation of the association, as we need both cases (with the disease) and controls (without the disease) to assess exposure rates in each group.

 

Option B. Only Online food eaters: This option focuses on the exposure rather than the outcome. A case-control study requires participants to be categorized by outcome (obesity or no obesity) rather than exposure. Selecting only online food eaters would not allow a clear comparison for the development of obesity based on differing exposure statuses.

 

Option D. Online food eaters and non-online food eaters: While this choice would work in a cohort study, it’s unsuitable for a case-control study. In a cohort study, the groups are divided based on exposure and followed over time to observe outcomes. Since the question specifies a case-control study, we need to focus on groups defined by the outcome (obesity status).

In a case-control study, groups should be selected based on the outcome (disease presence or absence), not the exposure. For this question, the appropriate groups are obese and non-obese individuals.

In this diagram, point A is the set cut-off value for the diagnostic test. Setting the cut-off at this position increases the ability of the test to correctly identify patients with cancer (True Positives) while reducing the number of False Negatives (patients who have cancer but are incorrectly identified as cancer-free).

 

When a cut-off is placed at a point that prioritizes detecting all true positive cases, it results in higher sensitivity. Sensitivity is defined as the test’s ability to correctly identify individuals with the disease. By capturing all true positive cases at this cut-off, the test becomes highly sensitive. However, this may slightly reduce specificity, as it could lead to more False Positives (patients without cancer who are incorrectly identified as having cancer).

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Low Sensitivity: Incorrect. Setting the cut-off at this point maximizes sensitivity, not reduces it.

 

Option C. Same Sensitivity and Specificity: Incorrect. Moving the cut-off increases sensitivity at the expense of specificity, so they are not equal.

 

Option D. High Specificity: Incorrect. High specificity would require a different cut-off point that minimizes False Positives, but point A is chosen to maximize True Positives, thereby enhancing sensitivity.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The cut-off point in diagnostic tests affects sensitivity and specificity. Setting a cut-off to capture all disease-positive cases increases sensitivity but may reduce specificity by allowing more False Positives.

questions.stem: Research is being conducted to find the association between aniline dye exposure and bladder cancer in workers who have worked in the industry for >20 years. Two groups were formed: one directly involved with dye handling and the other group consisting of office clerks not directly exposed to the dye. Years of occupation were noted from records. Then Bladder cancer cases were identified from both the groups in the current time. What type of study is being performed?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Retrospective cohort study

 

A retrospective cohort study involves identifying and dividing participants based on their past exposure to a certain factor (in this case, aniline dye) and then observing outcomes (such as bladder cancer) in the present time. Here, the study is set up by going back in time to identify workers who were either exposed to or not exposed to the dye based on past records (years of occupation). The researchers then come to the current time to observe who developed bladder cancer. This approach relies on historical data and moves forward to the present, making it retrospective in nature. The critical clue is that “years of occupation were noted from records,” indicating that the study setup and exposure were established from past data.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Prospective cohort study: This option is incorrect because, in a prospective cohort study, participants are followed forward in time from the point of exposure. Here, exposure is assessed retrospectively, and cancer cases are identified in the current time, not followed prospectively.

 

Option C. Case-control study: This option is incorrect because a case-control study starts with individuals who already have the disease (cases) and compares them to those who do not (controls), then looks backward to identify potential exposures. In this study, the cohort (groups of workers with or without exposure) was identified first, and then the outcome was determined, which is typical of a cohort study rather than a case-control design.

 

Option D. Intervention and response: This option is incorrect because an intervention study involves actively introducing an intervention to one group and comparing it with a control group to observe outcomes. In this study, no intervention was applied; it simply observes the correlation between past exposure and present disease status.

 

Educational Objective:

 

A retrospective cohort study identifies exposure status based on historical data and examines outcomes in the present, allowing calculation of incidence and relative risk.

questions.stemHtml: Given an image depicting various life stages, which vector is known for its ability to conduct transovarial transmission of the pathogen causing Scrub typhus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Trombiculid mite

 

  • Trombiculid mites, specifically the species Leptotrombidium deliense, are known for transmitting Scrub typhus, caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi.
  • These mites uniquely facilitate transovarial transmission, allowing the pathogen to be passed from the adult mite to its larvae.
  • This mechanism ensures that the larvae are already infectious when they first contact a host, bypassing the need for the larvae to acquire the pathogen through a blood meal.
  • Additionally, the larval stage acts as both a reservoir and a vector, a rare attribute in vector biology.

 

Other Options:
 

Option A. Hard tick - Known for transmitting Lyme disease and other pathogens, but primarily through blood meals rather than transovarial transmission for diseases like Scrub typhus.


Option B. Soft tick - Transmits pathogens like those causing Tick-borne relapsing fever, mainly through bites rather than transovarial transmission.


Option C. Louse - Transmits diseases such as typhus via direct contact and feces, not through transovarial transmission.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The Trombiculid mite’s ability to transmit Scrub typhus transovarially from the larval stage makes it an essential target for control measures in endemic regions.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man collapsed in a grocery store and was pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital. The autopsy was performed by a forensic expert at the medical college. During the legal proceedings to determine the cause of the incident, the attorney emphasized the absence of direct evidence proving negligence by the store staff but pointed to a legal doctrine suggesting that the facts of the case imply negligence. This doctrine, often applicable in such cases where the cause of an accident is known to the community but cannot be directly attributed, is a variant of which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Res ipsa loquitur

 

  • The doctrine of common knowledge is a variant of "Res ipsa loquitur," a Latin term meaning "the thing speaks for itself."
  • This legal principle is used in tort law when an accident's nature may not ordinarily occur in the absence of someone's negligence, and the evidence of the specific cause of injury is more accessible to the defendant than the plaintiff.
  • In this case, the collapse of a man in a grocery store without evident cause implies negligence that can be reasoned under this doctrine, particularly if no direct evidence of harm is available.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Medical maloccurence: Incorrect. This term typically refers to an unexpected medical event not necessarily related to negligence.

 

Option B. Novus actus interveniens: Incorrect. This refers to a new intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and thus relieves the defendant of liability, which is not applicable in this scenario.

 

Option D. Calculated risk doctrine: Incorrect. This legal concept involves risks that are acknowledged and accepted, often in a medical context, not relevant to this case.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • The doctrine of "Res ipsa loquitur" allows a plaintiff to prove negligence through the very nature of the accident or injury, assuming no direct evidence against the defendant, emphasizing that such incidents generally do not happen without negligence.
  • This doctrine is vital in forensic medical legal cases where direct evidence is lacking.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by the police after being involved in a physical altercation outside a local pub, where he allegedly broke another person's mandible. Considering the nature of the injury and the circumstances, which of the following actions is most appropriate for the police to take next?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Arrest without warrant

 

  • In cases of violent crimes such as assault leading to significant bodily harm (like a broken mandible), police in India have the authority to arrest the suspected individual without a warrant.
  • This is permissible under the Indian Penal Code, which allows law enforcement to take immediate action in the face of clear evidence of a cognizable offense where delay could compromise further investigation or the safety of any person.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Arrest with warrant:  Incorrect. While a warrant is typically required for arrests, exceptions include situations where immediate action is necessary to prevent further offenses or harm.

 

Option C. Declare him hostile: Incorrect. This term is used in court to describe a witness whose testimony goes against the interests of the party calling them, not applicable in the context of police actions immediately following a crime.

 

Option D. Put him in mental asylum: Incorrect. Mental asylums are for individuals diagnosed with severe mental disorders, and placement there requires medical and judicial review, not just police discretion following a criminal act.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • COGNISABLE OFFENCE (Sec 2(c) CrPC) -It is an offence in which a police officer can arrest a person without warrant from the magistrate, e.g., rape, murder, dowry death, ragging, death due to rash or negligent act, etc.
  •  In such offences, the individual is sent by the police to the doctor for medical examination (S.2C and 154 CrPC) 
  • In noncognisable offences, the injured person may go direct to the doctor, or he may file an affidavit in the Court of a Magistrate who will send him to the doctor for examination and report (S.41 CrPC).

Ans. D) Nd:YAG laser iridotomy

Option C. Diode laser transscleral cyclophotocoagulation: Diode laser cyclophotocoagulation is used to reduce intraocular pressure by destroying ciliary body tissue to decrease aqueous production. However, it is typically reserved for refractory glaucoma cases and not the first-line treatment for acute angle-closure glaucoma.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old male patient presents to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of gradual loss of peripheral vision in both eyes. On visual field testing, bitemporal hemianopia is observed. Which of the following is the most likely site of the lesion?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Optic chiasm

 

  • A lesion at the optic chiasm typically results in bitemporal hemianopia.
  • This occurs because the crossing fibers from the nasal halves of both retinas are affected, leading to loss of vision in the temporal fields of both eyes.
  • This pattern of visual field loss is commonly associated with pituitary tumors or other masses compressing the chiasm.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Optic nerve: A lesion of the optic nerve would lead to monocular vision loss in the affected eye, not bitemporal hemianopia.

 

Option C. Optic tract: A lesion in the optic tract results in contralateral homonymous hemianopia, where the same side of the visual field is lost in both eyes.

 

Option D. Lateral geniculate nucleus: A lesion in the lateral geniculate nucleus also causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia, similar to an optic tract lesion.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Bitemporal hemianopia is a visual field defect typically resulting from a lesion at the optic chiasm.
  • Monocular vision loss results from an optic nerve lesion.
  • Contralateral homonymous hemianopia can be caused by lesions in the optic tract or lateral geniculate nucleus.

questions.stem: A farmer came after snake bite on right foot. There were 2 fang marks with pain, swelling, and bleeding at the site of snake bite and the patient's vitals are stable. What will be the first step of management?

options.label: D
options.text: See the snake brought by the relatives

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Polyvalent Anti snake venom (ASV)

 

  • Based on the presence of two fang marks, pain, swelling, and bleeding at the site of the snake bite on the farmer's right foot, it is most likely a viper snake bite, which is poisonous.
  • The patient's vitals are stable, but the signs of envenomation are present.
  • In all cases of envenomation, the main life-treating measure is administering anti snake venom (ASV).
  • Polyvalent ASV 5000 units should be given as the first step in management whenever poisonous features, such as bleeding, are present.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Pressure immobilization: Immobilization is done for all snake bites, but, the Pressure immobilization is done for neurotoxic snakes but not for vasculotoxic snakes like vipers. Applying pressure in vasculotoxic snake bites can lead to local toxic effects and potentially result in limb amputation.

 

Option C. Venom suction: Venom suction is never an option in the management of snake bites.

 

Option D. See the snake brought by the relatives: Looking at the snake brought by relatives is rarely of practical use and is more of a theoretical consideration. It should not be the first step in managing a snake bite with signs of envenomation.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • In cases of snake bites with signs of envenomation, such as pain, swelling, and bleeding, administering polyvalent ASV should be the first step in management, regardless of the type of snake involved.

questions.stem: Two handkerchiefs with blood stains are found at a crime scene. What is the most appropriate procedure for handling these items?

options.label: A
options.text: Place them in same plastic bag and seal it for preservation

options.label: B
options.text: Preserve in envelope or paper bag

options.label: C
options.text: Fold the handkerchiefs in such a manner that the stained edges come together

options.label: D
options.text: Dry by spirit lamp to prevent putrefaction

questions.answerText: Preserve in envelope or paper bag
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Preserve in envelope or paper bag

 

  • When handling blood-stained handkerchiefs or any other stained items found at a crime scene, it is crucial to follow the appropriate procedure to ensure the preservation of evidence.
  • The most suitable method is to preserve the handkerchiefs in an envelope or paper bag, which allows for air circulation.
  • This prevents the growth of mold and bacteria that can occur when moisture is trapped in non-porous containers like plastic bags.
  • Additionally, it is important to dry the stains, but this should be done in the shade or by air drying.
  • Exposing the stains to direct sunlight or heat can denature the DNA, compromising the evidence.
  • Therefore, using a spirit lamp or any other heating material to dry the stains is not recommended.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Place them in same plastic bag and seal it for preservation: Plastic bags should be avoided as they can trap moisture, leading to the growth of mold and bacteria, which can compromise the evidence.

 

Option C. Fold the handkerchiefs in such a manner that the stained edges come together: Folding the handkerchiefs with the stained edges together can lead to the mixing of stains, making it difficult to distinguish between the stains from different individuals, if applicable.

 

Option D. Dry by spirit lamp to prevent putrefaction: Using a spirit lamp or any other heating material to dry the stains is not recommended, as it can denature the DNA and compromise the evidence. Drying should be done in the shade or by air drying.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • When handling blood-stained items found at a crime scene, preserve them in an envelope or paper bag to allow for air circulation, and dry the stains in the shade or by air drying to prevent DNA denaturation.
  • Avoid using plastic bags or exposing the stains to direct sunlight or heat.


ore, using a spirit lamp or any other heating material to dry the stains is not recommended.

questions.stem: According to the revised guidelines of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, under what circumstances can a pregnancy be terminated after 24 weeks?

Ans. C) Foetus malformation

  • In such cases, the opinion of the state medical board is required to proceed with the termination.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Rape: This option is incorrect because, while rape or sexual assault is one of the indications for MTP up to 24 weeks, it is not a specific indication for MTP beyond 24 weeks.

 

Option B. Contraceptive failure: This option is incorrect because contraceptive failure is a social indication for MTP up to 24 weeks, but it is not a specific indication for MTP beyond 24 weeks.

 

Option D. Insanity: This option is incorrect as it is not mentioned as an indication for MTP beyond 24 weeks.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • As per the new guidelines of the MTP Act in India, medical termination of pregnancy can be performed beyond 24 weeks of gestation only in cases of documented substantial fetal anomalies or malformations, and the opinion of the state medical board is required.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Stage 1 + stage 2

 

  • The demographic transition model consists of five stages, each characterized by different levels of crude birth rates (CBR) and crude death rates (CDR).
  • In stages 1 and 2, the birth rate remains high, while the death rate varies.

 

 

Stage 1 (High Stationary): In this stage, both the CBR (green line) and CDR (red line) are very high, resulting in a relatively stable population size.

 

Stage 2 (Early Expanding): The CBR remains high, but the CDR starts declining due to improvements in medical facilities, more hospitals, and more doctors. This leads to population growth.

 

Other Options:

 

In stage 3 (Late Expanding), the CBR starts declining for the first time due to the introduction of family planning programs, while the CDR continues to decrease. India is currently in this stage.

 

In stage 4 (Low Stationary), both the CBR and CDR are low, resulting in a stable population. This combination does not represent stages with the same birth rate but variable death rate.

 

In stage 5 (Declining), the CBR falls below the CDR, leading to population reduction. This combination does not represent stages with the same birth rate but variable death rate.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • In stages 1 and 2 of the demographic transition model, the crude birth rate remains high, while the crude death rate is high in stage 1 but starts declining in stage 2, making these the stages with the same birth rate but variable death rate.

questions.stem: Which of the following type of cataract is seen in ocular blunt trauma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Rosette cataract

 

  • A rosette cataract, also known as a traumatic cataract, is a specific type of cataract that can occur as a result of ocular blunt trauma.
  • When the eye experiences blunt trauma, such as a direct blow or impact, it can cause disruption or damage to the lens fibers.
  • This leads to the formation of a characteristic star-shaped opacity within the lens.
  • The term "rosette" refers to the appearance of the cataract, which resembles a flower-like pattern with radiating spokes or lines extending from a central point.

 

 

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Toxic cataract: This type of cataract is caused by exposure to toxic substances, such as certain medications, chemicals, or radiation. Unlike rosette cataracts, toxic cataracts are not associated with trauma but rather with harmful exposures.

 

Option B. Metabolic cataract: Metabolic cataracts develop due to systemic metabolic disorders, such as diabetes or galactosemia, which affect the metabolism of the lens proteins. These are not related to physical trauma to the eye.

 

Option D. Nuclear cataract: Nuclear cataract affects the central portion of the lens (nucleus) and is associated with aging. It causes gradual clouding and yellowing of the lens nucleus. This type of cataract is common in older adults but is not caused by trauma.

 

Educational Objective:

options.label: A
options.text: Sample size same as simple random

options.label: D
options.text: It is a method for rapid assessment

questions.answerText: Sample size same as simple random
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Sample size same as simple random

 

  • Cluster sampling is a two-stage sampling technique where clusters (e.g., villages or neighborhoods) are first selected, and then individuals within those clusters are sampled. 
  • While it is a cost-effective and efficient method for surveying large, geographically dispersed populations, it requires a larger sample size compared to simple random sampling to account for intra-cluster correlation, which reduces variability.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. It is two-stage sampling: This is correct. Cluster sampling involves selecting clusters first, followed by sampling individuals within those clusters, making it a two-stage process.

 

Option C. Cheaper than other methods: This is correct. Cluster sampling is more cost-effective than simple random sampling because it limits travel and logistical costs by focusing data collection within specific clusters.

 

Option D. It is a method for rapid assessment: This is correct. Cluster sampling is commonly used for rapid assessments in public health, such as vaccination coverage surveys, due to its efficiency in data collection.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Cluster sampling is a two-stage method used for efficient and cost-effective data collection. 
  • However, it requires a larger sample size than simple random sampling due to reduced variability within clusters.

questions.stem: Which graph is most appropriate to correlate two quantitative variables?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Scatter diagram

 

  • A scatter diagram (or scatter plot) is the most appropriate graph to show the correlation between two quantitative variables. 
  • It represents data points on a Cartesian plane, with one variable plotted on the x-axis and the other on the y-axis.
  •  Patterns in the plotted points reveal the nature of the relationship, such as positive, negative, or no correlation.
  •  This method is widely used in statistical analysis to visually assess the strength and direction of the relationship between two continuous variables.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Histogram: A histogram is used to display the frequency distribution of a single continuous variable, not to correlate two variables.

 

Option C. Line diagram: A line diagram is typically used to depict trends over time for a single variable. While it can show relationships indirectly, it is not specifically used for correlation between two variables.

 

Option D. Frequency curve: A frequency curve displays the distribution of a single variable's values and is not suitable for examining relationships between two variables.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • A scatter diagram is the best graphical tool for analyzing the correlation between two quantitative variables, providing a visual representation of the relationship and its direction.

questions.stem: Which procedure allows for the maximum correction of myopia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) LASIK

 

  • LASIK (Laser-Assisted in Situ Keratomileusis) is the most effective procedure for achieving the maximum correction of myopia.
  • This surgical technique utilizes a specialized laser to reshape the cornea, thereby correcting refractive errors that cause myopia.
  • LASIK is capable of correcting higher degrees of myopia more accurately and with quicker recovery times compared to other refractive surgeries. 
  • It provides significant long-term correction, often resulting in 20/25 vision or better for many patients.

 

Other Options: 

 

Option A. Radial keratotomy: Incorrect. Radial keratotomy was one of the earlier refractive surgeries used to treat myopia but is less precise than LASIK and generally used for lower degrees of myopia. It involves making radial cuts in the cornea to flatten it but has largely been superseded by newer technologies.

 

Option C. Photorefractive keratotomy: Incorrect. Photorefractive keratotomy (PRK) is similar to LASIK and also uses a laser to reshape the cornea. However, it tends to be chosen for patients with thinner corneas where creating a flap (as in LASIK) would be inappropriate. It generally corrects lower to moderate myopia better and has a longer recovery period compared to LASIK. 

 

Option D. Orthokeratology: Incorrect. Orthokeratology involves the use of specially designed contact lenses that temporarily reshape the cornea to reduce myopia. This method does not provide a permanent solution and requires ongoing use of the lenses to maintain the effect.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

  • LASIK surgery is the preferred and most effective method for the maximum and permanent correction of myopia compared to other available refractive procedures. 
  • Recognize the differences in application and efficacy between various methods of myopia correction.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Superior and lateral position of the eyeball

 

  • In ocular motor nerve (CN III) palsy, typical findings include ptosis (drooping of the upper eyelid) and pupillary dilatation due to paralysis of the iris sphincter muscle. 
  • An absent light reflex can also be observed due to the impaired pupillary constriction in response to light. 
  • However, the characteristic position of the eyeball in CN III palsy is "down and out," where the eye is positioned downward and laterally due to unopposed action of the lateral rectus (controlled by CN VI) and superior oblique (controlled by CN IV) muscles. 
  • Thus, a "superior and lateral position of the eyeball" is not seen in CN III palsy and is incorrect.

 

Educational Objective:

Ans. B) Perform ear irrigation with warm water

Option D. Refer to an otolaryngologist for immediate removal: Referral is unnecessary as a first-line step in most cases of cerumen impaction. Primary care providers can usually manage this condition effectively unless complications or failed initial treatment necessitate specialist intervention.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man presents to the clinic with a 2-month history of nasal obstruction, epistaxis, and a sensation of fullness in his right ear. He also reports recurrent headaches and neck swelling. He has a history of smoking and significant alcohol consumption. On examination, there is a mass in the nasopharynx and right-sided cervical lymphadenopathy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Nasopharyngeal carcinoma

 

  • Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a malignant tumor originating in the nasopharynx. 
  • It commonly presents with nasal obstruction, epistaxis, unilateral ear symptoms (such as fullness or hearing loss), headaches, and cervical lymphadenopathy. 
  • Risk factors include smoking, alcohol consumption, and Epstein-Barr virus infection. 
  • The combination of symptoms and findings in this patient strongly suggests NPC.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Allergic rhinitis: Allergic rhinitis typically presents with nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, sneezing, and itching. It does not cause epistaxis, a mass in the nasopharynx, or cervical lymphadenopathy.

 

Option B. Chronic sinusitis: Chronic sinusitis may present with nasal obstruction and headache but is not associated with epistaxis, a nasopharyngeal mass, or cervical lymphadenopathy. The sensation of ear fullness in chronic sinusitis is usually bilateral and related to sinus congestion.

 

Option D. Benign nasal polyp: Benign nasal polyps can cause nasal obstruction and fullness but are not typically associated with epistaxis, recurrent headaches, or cervical lymphadenopathy.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Nasopharyngeal carcinoma should be suspected in patients with nasal obstruction, epistaxis, unilateral ear symptoms, and cervical lymphadenopathy, especially in those with risk factors like smoking and alcohol consumption. 
  • Early recognition is essential for timely diagnosis and treatment.

questions.stem: A group of fishermen in a remote village rely heavily on a diet of rice and fish, with limited access to fresh fruits or vegetables. Over time, they begin experiencing difficulty in walking, leg pain, and need support to stand. Which vitamin supplementation could have helped prevent these symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Vitamin C

 

  • The symptoms described are indicative of scurvy, which results from a deficiency in Vitamin C.
  • Vitamin C is essential for the synthesis of collagen, a structural protein critical for the maintenance of healthy skin, blood vessels, and bones.
  • Without adequate Vitamin C, collagen formation is impaired, leading to symptoms such as joint pain, leg weakness, and difficulties in walking due to weakened connective tissue.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Vitamin A: Deficiency in Vitamin A primarily affects vision and immune function, but it does not lead to the musculoskeletal symptoms described here.

 

Option B. Vitamin D: A deficiency in Vitamin D can cause bone pain and muscle weakness, but it is more likely associated with conditions like rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

 

Option D. Vitamin B: Deficiency in certain B vitamins can lead to conditions such as anemia and peripheral neuropathy, but it does not typically cause collagen-related symptoms like those seen in scurvy.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Vitamin C deficiency can lead to scurvy, a condition characterized by collagen maturation defects, which can cause symptoms such as leg pain, difficulty walking, and the need for physical support.

questions.stem: In a medical malpractice case, under which legal doctrine does the burden of proof for the defense primarily lie with the doctor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Res ipsa loquitur

 

  • The legal doctrine of Res ipsa loquitur translates to "the thing speaks for itself." 
  • In cases involving Res ipsa loquitur, the burden of proof may shift to the defendant, in this case, the doctor, to prove that there was no negligence. 
  • This doctrine is applicable when an injury occurs under circumstances that ordinarily would not happen without negligence, and the plaintiff may not have direct evidence of the doctor's fault. 
  • Thus, the doctor is required to provide evidence that they exercised the necessary standard of care.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Mens rea: Mens rea refers to the mental state or intent behind an action, typically in criminal law. It is not applicable to civil cases of medical negligence, where intent is not a primary factor.

 

Option C. Res judicata: Res judicata means "a matter already judged" and prevents the same case from being tried again once a final judgment has been made. It does not involve shifting the burden of proof to the doctor in malpractice cases.

 

Option D. Respondeat superior: Respondeat superior is a legal doctrine holding an employer or principal legally responsible for the actions of an employee or agent, performed within the scope of their employment. This does not shift the burden of proof to the doctor in a malpractice case.

  • In cases involving Res ipsa loquitur, the burden of proof may shift to the doctor to demonstrate that they were not negligent, as the circumstances themselves suggest an assumption of negligence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a patency test of the eustachian tube?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Cottle test

 

  • The Cottle test is used to assess nasal valve patency, not eustachian tube function. 
  • During this test, the examiner pulls the cheek away from the midline, which increases airflow from that side of the nasal cavity if the nasal valve is functional. 
  • It is used to diagnose issues related to nasal obstruction, not eustachian tube patency.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Politzer Test: This is used primarily for children. During the test, a Politzer bag is used to introduce air pressure into the nose while keeping the nose and mouth closed. The patient is instructed to swallow, and if the eustachian tube is patent, a hissing sound can be heard.

 

Option B. Sonotubometry: This test involves sending a sound signal through the nose and the external auditory canal (EAC). If the eustachian tube is patent, the sound will be louder when heard through the EAC. This test is still under development in some areas.

 

Option D. Toynbee Test: In this test, the patient swallows while the nose is closed. This leads to retraction of the tympanic membrane (TM) on otoscopy, indicating that the eustachian tube is patent.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • The Cottle test is used for assessing nasal valve patency and not for evaluating eustachian tube function. 
  • The other listed tests (Politzer, Sonotubometry, and Toynbee) are specific tests used to evaluate eustachian tube patency.

questions.stem: A patient is undergoing intraocular pressure measurement using applanation tonometry. Which of the following corneal conditions would most likely lead to an inaccurately high intraocular pressure reading?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Thick cornea

 

  • Applanation tonometry measures intraocular pressure (IOP) by flattening the cornea. 
  • The thickness of the cornea influences the measurement: a thicker cornea resists flattening more than a normal or thin cornea, which can lead to an artificially high reading.
  • This is a result of the increased resistance provided by the extra corneal tissue, which the tonometer interprets as higher IOP.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Thin cornea: A thin cornea is likely to yield an inaccurately low IOP reading because it requires less force to flatten. Therefore, thin corneas are associated with underestimation of intraocular pressure, not overestimation.

 

Option C. Edematous cornea: Corneal edema can make the cornea more compliant and less rigid, potentially causing variations in IOP measurements. However, it typically leads to underestimation rather than overestimation of IOP.

 

Option D. Keratoconus: Keratoconus is a condition where the cornea thins and becomes conical. Due to this abnormal shape and thinness, applanation tonometry measurements can underestimate IOP in keratoconic eyes rather than overestimate it.

 

Educational Objective:

 

A thick cornea can lead to an overestimation of intraocular pressure during applanation tonometry due to increased resistance to flattening.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient presents with double vision and impaired horizontal eye movements. On examination, adduction of one eye is impaired, while the contralateral eye shows nystagmus on abduction. Which neural structure is most likely involved in causing this internuclear ophthalmoplegia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Medial longitudinal bundle

 

  • Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) is characterized by impaired horizontal eye movement, with an inability to adduct one eye and nystagmus of the abducting eye. 
  • This condition results from a lesion in the medial longitudinal bundle (MLB), a neural pathway that coordinates eye movements by connecting the abducens nucleus of one side with the oculomotor nucleus of the other. 
  • The MLB is crucial for the horizontal gaze conjugation, and lesions here commonly occur in demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Pontine reticular formation: This area is involved in coordinating rapid eye movements but does not directly cause internuclear ophthalmoplegia. Lesions here are associated with gaze palsies rather than INO.

 

Option C. Cerebellum: While the cerebellum plays a role in coordination and balance, it is not directly involved in eye movement coordination through the medial longitudinal bundle. Cerebellar lesions typically affect saccadic movements and smooth pursuit rather than causing INO.

 

Option D. Motor nuclear sparing Edinger-Westphal nucleus: The Edinger-Westphal nucleus is part of the oculomotor complex and is primarily responsible for pupillary constriction and lens accommodation. It does not play a role in the horizontal gaze pathway associated with the MLB and thus is not involved in INO.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) results from a lesion in the medial longitudinal bundle (MLB), which disrupts coordinated eye movement and is commonly seen in multiple sclerosis.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man is admitted to the hospital following a severe motor vehicle accident. Despite initial stabilization, he succumbs to his injuries three days after the incident. During the postmortem examination, bleeding is noted on the surface of the brain that does not wash away with water. Which of the following is the most likely source of this bleeding?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Subarachnoid bleeding

 

  • Subarachnoid bleeding, or subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), is the accumulation of blood within the subarachnoid space, where cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) normally circulates. 
  • When a person experiences head trauma, blood from damaged vessels in this space may accumulate. 
  • During a postmortem examination, blood in the subarachnoid space typically remains intact, not easily washed away by water, due to its location within the layers of the meninges. 
  • This feature of subarachnoid bleeding helps differentiate it from other types of intracranial hemorrhages, which can often be displaced by washing. 
  • Traumatic SAH is common in head injuries and is often associated with significant morbidity and mortality.

 

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Epidural bleeding: Epidural hemorrhage occurs between the dura mater and the skull and is typically caused by an arterial rupture, often due to temporal bone fractures that damage the middle meningeal artery. The blood from an epidural hemorrhage is usually contained in a biconvex shape on imaging and can sometimes be washed away by water in a postmortem setting, unlike subarachnoid bleeding.

 

Option C. Subdural hematoma (SDH): Subdural hematoma occurs between the dura and arachnoid mater and is often associated with venous bleeding, particularly from bridging veins. While subdural blood can adhere to the surface of the brain, it is typically displaced more easily than subarachnoid blood during postmortem washing, which helps distinguish it from subarachnoid hemorrhage.

 

Option D. Intraparenchymal bleeding: Intraparenchymal or intracerebral bleeding occurs within the brain tissue itself, rather than on its surface or in the subarachnoid space. This type of hemorrhage is typically confined within the brain parenchyma and can be washed away if exposed to water during an autopsy, unlike subarachnoid hemorrhage.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Subarachnoid hemorrhage can be identified postmortem by blood that remains intact and is not washed away by water, distinguishing it from other types of intracranial bleeding.

Ans. D) Hemodilution from absorbed freshwater, leading to an electrolyte imbalance

His stapedial reflex was checked and it was present. Schirmer’s test for lacrimation was done, and it was negative (i.e., lacrimation was normal). options.label: A
options.text: Trans labyrinthine portion (the portion of the facial nerve lying at the level of the inner ear)

options.text: Horizontal portion of the facial nerve on the medial wall of the middle ear

  • Damage to the facial nerve in this portion can lead to absent taste sensation because the chorda tympani nerve (which carries taste sensation from the anterior 2/3rd of the tongue) arises below this segment. 
  • The presence of a normal stapedial reflex and lacrimation indicates that the lesion is distal to the fibers for lacrimation and stapedial muscle innervation.

questions.stem: A patient presents with an acute onset of severe eye pain and a noticeable reduction in vision. On examination, the pupil appears mid-dilated and vertically oval. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Angle closure glaucoma

 

  • Angle closure glaucoma is characterized by a sudden increase in intraocular pressure due to a closure of the drainage angle between the iris and the cornea. 
  • This blockage leads to rapid eye pressure buildup, causing symptoms such as severe eye pain, headache, nausea, and acute vision loss. 
  • The vertically oval shape of the pupil in acute attacks is indicative of iris sphincter muscle ischemia caused by elevated intraocular pressures.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. CSR/Macular degeneration: Typically presents with painless vision loss, not associated with changes in pupil shape or acute pain.

 

Option B. Cataract: Leads to gradual vision loss with clouding of the lens and does not cause sudden pain or pupil distortion.

 

Option C. Optic neuritis: Causes sudden onset vision loss associated with painful eye movements, but is not associated with oval pupil changes and does not result in acute intraocular pressure rise.

 

Educational Objective: 

 

  • In cases of sudden painful vision loss with a vertically oval pupil, angle closure glaucoma should be considered a critical emergency requiring immediate intervention to prevent irreversible damage to the optic nerve and permanent vision loss.

During the postmortem examination, the forensic expert notices a peculiar color change on the bodies. Considering the likely cause of death is related to inhalation of smoke and toxic gases produced from woodfire, which of the following findings is most likely to be seen?

  • When a fire occurs in a closed space (home), the combustion is incomplete due to limited oxygen. 
  • This leads to the production of carbon monoxide (CO). 
  • Carbon monoxide binds with hemoglobin in the blood to form carboxyhemoglobin, which imparts a characteristic cherry red color to the hypostasis seen in the body post-mortem. 
  • This is a hallmark finding in CO poisoning and is used as a key diagnostic indicator.
  • Additionally, fires in industrial buildings (closed spaces) can produce cyanide due to the combustion of synthetic fibers containing nitrogen.

Note - Fire in open space – the combustion is complete due to presence of sufficient oxygen, leads to production of CO2.

Option C. Blackish discoloration: Blackish discoloration is typically associated with carbonization or burning of the body tissues, not with carbon monoxide or cyanide poisoning. This option is incorrect in the context of the given scenario.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is the correct way to calculate the current annual growth rate of a population?

options.label: A
options.text: Crude birth rate (CBR) minus Crude death rate (CDR)

options.label: B
options.text: Crude death rate (CDR) minus Crude birth rate (CBR)

options.label: D
options.text: Crude birth rate (CBR) plus Crude death rate (CDR)

questions.answerText: Crude birth rate (CBR) minus Crude death rate (CDR)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Crude birth rate (CBR) minus Crude death rate (CDR)

 

  • The current annual growth rate of a population is calculated as the difference between the Crude Birth Rate (CBR) and the Crude Death Rate (CDR). 
  • This formula gives an estimate of how much the population is increasing or decreasing each year, expressed as a percentage:

      Annual Growth Rate = CBR – CDR

  • Further for expression as a percentage divide the calculated value by 10 (as CBR, CDR are expressed as per 1000 mid-year population each)

 

Educational Objective:

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding ecological studies is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: They provide the strongest evidence for causality between exposure and outcome

options.label: B
options.text: The units of analysis in ecological studies are individuals rather than populations

options.label: C
options.text: Ecological fallacy refers to incorrectly attributing group-level associations to individuals

options.label: D
options.text: They are expensive and require extensive time to collect primary data

questions.answerText: Ecological fallacy refers to incorrectly attributing group-level associations to individuals
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Ecological fallacy refers to incorrectly attributing group-level associations to individuals.

 

  • Option C is correct because an ecological fallacy occurs when conclusions drawn from population-level data are incorrectly applied to individuals. 
  • For example, just because a country with higher average alcohol consumption has higher heart disease mortality rates does not mean that individuals who drink more alcohol in that country are more likely to die of heart disease. 
  • This is a common pitfall in ecological studies.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. They provide the strongest evidence for causality between exposure and outcome: Incorrect. Ecological studies provide the least satisfactory evidence for causality among observational study designs. They are useful for generating hypotheses but are limited in establishing causal relationships due to confounding factors.

 

Option B. The units of analysis in ecological studies are individuals rather than populations: Incorrect. The units of analysis in an ecological study are populations or groups, not individuals. For example, an ecological study might analyze average alcohol consumption and mortality rates at the national level.

 

Option D. They are expensive and require extensive time to collect primary data: Incorrect. One of the advantages of ecological studies is that they can be conducted quickly and inexpensively because they use pre-existing population-level data (secondary data) rather than requiring the collection of new data from individuals.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Ecological studies use population-level data to assess associations between exposures and outcomes.
  • They are cost-effective and time-efficient but provide limited evidence for causality.
  • The ecological fallacy is a key limitation, where group-level findings are mistakenly applied to individuals, leading to misinterpretation of results.

On examination, the tympanic membrane appears red and bulging, and there is reduced mobility of the membrane on pneumatic otoscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Acute suppurative otitis media

 

  • Acute suppurative otitis media is a bacterial infection of the middle ear, typically seen in children, often following an upper respiratory infection. 
  • Clinical features include fever, ear pain, irritability, and a red, bulging tympanic membrane on otoscopy. 
  • Pneumatic otoscopy often shows decreased mobility due to the accumulation of pus behind the tympanic membrane. 
  • Common bacterial pathogens include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis.
  • Treatment often involves antibiotics, especially if symptoms persist or worsen.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Otitis externa: It involves inflammation or infection of the external ear canal, often caused by bacteria or fungi. It presents with ear pain, itching, and discharge but does not involve a bulging tympanic membrane or middle ear infection.

 

Option B. Chronic otitis media: It refers to a long-standing infection of the middle ear with perforation of the tympanic membrane and discharge (otorrhea). It lacks the acute features of fever and ear pain seen in acute suppurative otitis media.

 

Option D. Serous otitis media: Also called otitis media with effusion is characterized by the presence of non-infected fluid in the middle ear. The tympanic membrane may appear dull and retracted rather than bulging and red. It often follows an acute infection but does not cause fever or significant ear pain.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Acute suppurative otitis media is a common bacterial infection in children, characterized by fever, ear pain, and a bulging, erythematous tympanic membrane. 
  • Early diagnosis and treatment with antibiotics can prevent complications such as tympanic membrane perforation or mastoiditis.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy presents to the ophthalmology clinic with a history of persistent tearing from his right eye for over a year. His parents report that the tearing has not improved despite performing daily lacrimal sac massage as recommended by a previous physician. On examination, there is noticeable tearing with no signs of inflammation or discharge, and the tear drainage test indicates nasolacrimal duct obstruction. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Dacryocystorhinostomy

 

  • Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) is the indicated treatment for chronic nasolacrimal duct obstruction in children older than 2 years who have failed conservative management. 
  • This procedure involves creating a new passage for tears between the lacrimal sac and the nasal cavity, effectively bypassing the blocked nasolacrimal duct.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Nasolacrimal duct massage: Although effective in young infants, particularly under 6-8 weeks of age, it is unlikely to be successful in resolving chronic obstruction in an older child after prolonged conservative management.

 

Option C. Syringing and Probing: It is effective in younger children around 18-24 months year age and used as a second-line treatment after failed relief from nasolacrimal duct massage but is not effective in persistent cases or older children.

 

Option D. Lacrimal sac massage: Similar to nasolacrimal duct massage, it is effective in infants and used as a first-line treatment but is not effective in persistent cases or older children.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • For a child with chronic nasolacrimal duct obstruction who has failed initial conservative measures, Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) is the recommended treatment. 
  • DCR provides a new pathway for tear drainage, helping to relieve symptoms of epiphora in patients for whom conservative management is no longer effective.
