questions.stem: Which of the following factors does not directly influence the calculation of the standard deviation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Median

 

  • Standard deviation is a measure of the spread or dispersion of a set of data points relative to their mean.
  • It directly depends on the mean because it involves the calculation of the average distance of each data point from the mean.
  • It also depends on the range and sample size since they affect the distribution and spread of the data.
  • However, the median does not directly influence the standard deviation because the median is a measure of central tendency that does not take into account the distances of data points from the mean.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Mean: The standard deviation calculation involves the mean, as it measures how much the data points deviate from the mean.

 

Option C. Range: While not directly used in the formula, the range gives an indication of the spread of the data, which is related to the standard deviation.

 

Option D. Sample size: The sample size affects the standard deviation, especially when calculating the standard error, as it is used in the denominator of the formula.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • The standard deviation is influenced by the mean, range, and sample size but not by the median, as the median is a measure of central tendency that does not consider the spread of data points around the mean.

  • Marshall’s triad, in the context of bomb explosions, refers to the combination of bruises, abrasions, and punctate lacerations with tattooing from explosive materials.

  • The force of the blast can propel debris and explosive materials at high velocity, causing these characteristic injury patterns on the skin.

questions.stem: A 2-week-old infant is brought in for a routine eye examination. The pediatrician notes that the infant's eyes appear structurally normal, but the refractive status needs to be assessed. What is the most likely refractive status of this newborn?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Hypermetropic

 

  • Newborns are typically hypermetropic (farsighted) with a refractive error of approximately +2 to +3 diopters.
  • This hypermetropia is due to the shorter anteroposterior diameter of the eye at birth, which is about 16.5 mm, roughly 70% of the adult size.
  • The corneal horizontal diameter is also smaller, around 9.5 to 10 mm, and the anterior chamber is shallow.
  • These anatomical characteristics contribute to the hypermetropic refractive status seen in most newborns.
  • As the child grows, the eye's axial length increases, which may reduce hypermetropia or lead to emmetropia (normal vision).

 

Other Options

 

Option A. Myopic: Myopia (near-sightedness) is uncommon in newborns; their shorter axial length typically results in hypermetropia.

 

Option C. Astigmatic: While astigmatism can occur, hypermetropia is the more common refractive status at birth.

 

Option D. Emmetropic: Newborns are generally not emmetropic; they typically present with hypermetropia.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • The most common refractive status of a newborn is hypermetropia, primarily due to the shorter anteroposterior diameter and other anatomical features of the eye at birth.

questions.stem: Which of the following findings is not typically associated with oculomotor nerve palsy?

options.label: C
options.text: Superior and lateral position of the eyeball

questions.answerText: Superior and lateral position of the eyeball
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Superior and lateral position of the eyeball

 

  • In oculomotor nerve palsy, the affected eye typically moves downward and outward (inferior and lateral position) due to the unopposed action of the lateral rectus and superior oblique muscles, which are innervated by the abducens and trochlear nerves, respectively.
  • The superior and lateral position of the eyeball is not characteristic of oculomotor nerve palsy.
  • Other common features of oculomotor nerve palsy include ptosis (drooping of the eyelid) due to paralysis of the levator palpebrae superioris, pupillary dilatation (mydriasis) due to the loss of parasympathetic innervation, and an absent light reflex.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Ptosis: Ptosis occurs because the oculomotor nerve innervates the levator palpebrae superioris muscle, which elevates the eyelid.

 

Option B. Pupillary dilatation: The oculomotor nerve carries parasympathetic fibers responsible for constricting the pupil, so its palsy results in a dilated pupil.

 

Option D. Light reflex absent: The oculomotor nerve is involved in the pupillary light reflex; its palsy can lead to an absent light reflex on the affected side.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Oculomotor nerve palsy typically causes ptosis, pupillary dilatation, and an eye positioned downward and outward.
  • A superior and lateral position of the eyeball is not seen in this condition.

questions.stemHtml: A 22-year-old female presents with pain and swelling in front of the right ear for 2 days. She has had a similar episode in the past 3 years. The image provided shows the clinical finding. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Infected preauricular sinus

 

  • Preauricular sinus is a congenital condition where there is a small pit or tract located near the front of the ear.
  • These sinuses are prone to infection due to the accumulation of debris, leading to pain, swelling, and purulent discharge, as seen in the provided image.
  • The recurring nature of the infection further supports this diagnosis.

 

Option A. Preauricular cellulitis: While this condition causes pain and swelling around the ear, it lacks the hallmark pit or sinus tract associated with preauricular sinuses. The image shows a clear sinus with discharge, which is not typical of cellulitis alone.

 

Option B. Infected branchial cleft cyst: This is typically located in the lateral neck, not in front of the ear. Although it may present with similar symptoms, the location and appearance in this case are inconsistent with a branchial cleft cyst.

 

Option D. Sebaceous cyst with secondary infection: Sebaceous cysts can become infected and form abscesses. However, these are usually not located near the ear and would not show the characteristic preauricular pit that leads to recurring infections.

Infected preauricular sinus presents with recurrent painful swelling and purulent discharge near the ear due to a congenital pit or tract. It is a common diagnosis in patients with such symptoms.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old male with uncontrolled diabetes presents with ear pain and otorrhea for the last 2 weeks. Otoscopic examination reveals granulation tissue at the bony-cartilaginous junction of the external auditory canal (EAC). What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: D
options.text: External auditory canal squamous cell carcinoma

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Malignant otitis externa

 

  • This is a severe, necrotizing infection of the external auditory canal that primarily affects elderly diabetics and immunocompromised individuals.
  • It is caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa in most cases.
  • The hallmark findings are severe pain, otorrhea, and granulation tissue at the bony-cartilaginous junction of the EAC, as described in this case.
  • Without treatment, the infection can spread to adjacent bones and soft tissues, leading to life-threatening complications like skull base osteomyelitis.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Fungal otitis externa (Otomycosis): Fungal infections typically present with ear discharge that has a characteristic "fluffy" appearance, often due to fungal elements like Aspergillus or Candida. However, granulation tissue is not a typical finding in otomycosis, and this condition is usually more benign compared to malignant otitis externa.

 

Option C. Acute suppurative otitis media (ASOM): ASOM involves infection of the middle ear, not the external ear canal. It is associated with fever, otalgia, and a bulging tympanic membrane due to pus buildup behind the eardrum, which is different from the findings described in this patient.

 

Option D. Squamous cell carcinoma of the external auditory canal: This is a rare and aggressive tumor that can present similarly with otorrhea and pain. However, the granulation tissue seen in this case, along with the patient's diabetic history, is more indicative of an infectious rather than a neoplastic process.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Malignant otitis externa, a life-threatening infection often seen in uncontrolled diabetics, presents with granulation tissue at the junction of the bony and cartilaginous external auditory canal, severe pain, and otorrhea.

Perform myringotomy with grommet insertion to relieve middle ear pressure and facilitate drainage: Myringotomy with grommet insertion is a treatment to relieve pressure and drain fluid in cases of otitis media with effusion, but it may not be the initial step especially if nasopharyngeal pathology is suspected.

 

Option C. Instruct the patient to perform the Valsalva maneuver, which can sometimes open the Eustachian tube to equalize middle ear pressure: The Valsalva maneuver is a simple technique to potentially open the Eustachian tube and equalize pressure but is usually ineffective in resolving fluid in the middle ear when there is underlying pathology.

 

Option D. Prescribe antihistaminics, assuming the effusion might be related to allergic etiologies: Antihistaminics may be used in the treatment of allergic conditions that can lead to Eustachian tube dysfunction, but they are not the primary modality of investigation or treatment in the presence of unilateral effusion in an adult.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Nasopharyngeal pathology can be diagnosed with endoscopic examination in an adult patient with unilateral serous otitis media, as it may be indicative of serious underlying conditions that could lead to Eustachian tube dysfunction and middle ear effusion.

questions.stemHtml: A researcher is reviewing a study that analyzed the body temperature of different age groups. The study utilized a graphical representation to summarize the distribution of temperatures across various age decades. Refering to the graph provided, which type of statistical diagram is used to display the body temperature across age groups?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Box and Whisker plot

 

  • The diagram shown is a Box and Whisker plot, also known as a box plot.
  • It is a standardized way of displaying the distribution of data based on a five-number summary: minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3), and maximum.
  • It can also show outliers and the symmetry or skewness of the distribution.
  • In the provided graphic, the boxes represent the interquartile range (the middle 50% of data), the line within the box marks the median, and the 'whiskers' indicate variability outside the upper and lower quartiles.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Funnel plot is used to detect bias or systematic errors in meta-analyses and can show the relationship between treatment effect and study size.

 

Option B. Forest plot is often used in systematic reviews and meta-analyses to show estimates from different studies.

 

Option C. Stem and Leaf plot is a graphical representation that is used to display quantitative data to retain the original data while showing it graphically.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  •  
  • Line in Box: 2nd Quartile (Median)
  • Whiskers end: Minimum & Maximum Values
  • Edges of box: 1st and 3rd Quartile

The researchers plotted the oximeter readings without micropore against those with micropore applied. Based on the scatter plot provided, what inference can be made about the relationship between pulse oximeter readings with and without micropore in neonates?

options.label: A
options.text: There is a positive correlation with a constant 3% increase in Y-axis value.

options.label: B
options.text: There is a constant negative correlation between two variables.

options.label: C
options.text: There is a constant positive correlation between two variables.

options.label: D
options.text: There is no correlation between the two variables.

questions.answerText: There is a constant positive correlation between two variables.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) There is a constant positive correlation between two variables.

 

  • The scatter plot shows a collection of data points that appear to have a positive trend, indicating that as one variable increases, so does the other.
  • This pattern suggests a positive correlation between the two variables, with no indication from the plot that the increase in the Y-axis value is exactly 3% or constant; rather, it shows a general trend without specifying the exact rate of increase.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. There is a positive correlation with a constant 3% increase in Y-axis value: The scatter plot does not provide evidence of a "constant 3% increase" in the Y-axis value; thus, we cannot confirm this choice solely based on the plot.

 

Option B. There is a constant negative correlation between two variables: A negative correlation would mean that as one variable increases, the other decreases. This is not the case here, as the scatter plot shows a positive trend.

 

Option D. There is no correlation between the two variables: If there were no correlation, we would expect to see a much more random distribution of data points, which is not depicted here.

 

Educational Objective:

 

PEARSON CORRELATION COEFFICIENT (r)

 

  •  
  • A value of r = 0 indicates that there is no association between the two variables.
  • A value 0 < r < +1 indicates a positive association; that is, as the value of one variable increases, so does the value of the other variable.
  • A value – 1 < r < 0 indicates a negative association; that is, as the value of one variable increases, the value of the other variable decreases.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old female patient presents with gradual, progressive visual field loss in both eyes. Examination reveals increased intraocular pressure, cupping of the optic disc, and visual field testing shows arcuate scotoma. Which cell type in the retina is primarily affected in this patient's condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Ganglion cells

 

  • Ganglion cells are the final output neurons of the vertebrate retina.
  • They are primarily affected in glaucomatous optic atrophy, leading to characteristic optic nerve changes and visual field loss.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Amacrine cells: Amacrine cells are interneurons in the retina that process visual information. They are not primarily affected in glaucomatous optic atrophy.

 

Option B. Bipolar cells: Bipolar cells are also interneurons in the retina and serve as a relay between photoreceptors and ganglion cells. They are not the initial cell type affected in glaucoma.

 

Option D. Rods and cones: Rods and cones are the photoreceptor cells in the retina responsible for light detection and image formation. They are not directly affected by the elevated intraocular pressure in glaucoma.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Glaucomatous optic atrophy primarily affects retinal ganglion cells, leading to their apoptosis and resulting in progressive optic nerve changes and visual field defects.

questions.stem: A medical resident is participating in a forensic rotation and is presented with a challenging task. The resident needs to analyze a degraded blood sample collected from an old crime scene to confirm the presence of hemoglobin. Given the sample's condition, it's crucial to use a forensic test that can provide specific microscopic evidence to ensure the result's accuracy. The resident must select the most appropriate test to observe the characteristic findings that would confirm haemoglobin’s presence. Which test should the medical resident utilize to observe the characteristic pink feathery crystals that confirm the presence of hemoglobin in the degraded blood sample?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Takayama test

 

  • The Takayama test is a forensic chemical test specifically designed to confirm the presence of hemoglobin in blood samples.
  • This test is known for producing characteristic pink feathery crystals, known as hemochromogen crystals, when the sample reacts with pyridine and sodium hydroxide.
  • These distinctive microscopic findings provide a reliable indication of hemoglobin's presence, making the Takayama test particularly useful in forensic analysis of blood, even in degraded samples.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Teichmann test: This test also confirms the presence of hemoglobin but results in the formation of brownish crystals of hemin chloride, not pink feathery crystals.

 

Option C. Barbario’s test: This is not a recognized standard test for the detection of hemoglobin in forensic science.

 

Option D. Xanthoproteic test: This test is used to detect the presence of aromatic amino acids in proteins by producing a yellow color upon reaction with nitric acid and is not specific to hemoglobin detection.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Microchemical tests for Blood: Teichmann’s and Takayama test (Both are confirmatory tests)
  • Teichmann’s - Brownish-black rhombic crystals of hematin chloride
  • Takayama test - Pink feathery crystals of hemochromogen (reduced alkaline hematin)
  • Microchemical tests for Semen: Florence and Barberio test (Both are presumptive tests)
  • Florence test—For choline (dark brown rhombic crystals)
  • Barberio test— detects spermine (yellow needle-shaped rhombic crystals)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the diagnosis of an infant with PHPV?

options.label: A
options.text: PHPV is the result of failure of regression of fetal vasculature and can present as leukocoria.

options.label: B
options.text: PHPV is frequently associated with Down syndrome.

options.label: C
options.text: Anterior PHPV generally has a poor prognosis due to the high likelihood of amblyopia.

options.label: D
options.text: Calcification is a common finding in PHPV and should be expected in this case.

questions.answerText: PHPV is the result of failure of regression of fetal vasculature and can present as leukocoria.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) PHPV is the result of failure of regression of fetal vasculature and can present as leukocoria.

 

  • True, PHPV is a developmental anomaly that occurs due to the failure of the fetal hyaloid artery to regress and can present with leukocoria (true white pupil).

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. PHPV is frequently associated with Down syndrome: False, PHPV is not associated with Down syndrome, but rather can be associated with Patau syndrome (trisomy 13).

 

Option C. Anterior PHPV generally has a poor prognosis due to the high likelihood of amblyopia: False, anterior PHPV generally has a good prognosis if managed appropriately, with the risk of amblyopia being the primary concern.

 

Option D. Calcification is a common finding in PHPV and should be expected in this case: False, calcification is not typically seen in PHPV; it is more commonly associated with retinoblastoma.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous (PHPV) is a non-hereditary, congenital anomaly due to the failure of the fetal hyaloid artery to regress, often presenting unilaterally with leukocoria, and is associated with a good prognosis when anterior without calcification.

Educational Objective:

 

  • The feathery hyphae and finger-like projections of a corneal ulcer with minimal hypopyon are indicative of Aspergillosis, a fungal cause of keratitis, particularly in the setting of vegetative injury

questions.stemHtml: A researcher is examining three different population samples to estimate the average effect of a new drug. The graph presents three normal distributions of sample means with varying sample sizes: 1 (n = 1000), 2 (n = 800), and 3 (n = 600). Based on the information provided, which order correctly represents the margin of error from greatest to least among the three samples?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) 3>2>1

 

  • The margin of error is inversely related to the sample size; therefore, a larger sample size results in a smaller margin of error.
  • This is due to the central limit theorem, which states that as sample size increases, the sampling distribution of the sample mean will be more closely approximated by a normal distribution with a smaller spread.
  • Given the sample sizes provided, the sample with n=600 (3) would have the largest margin of error, followed by the sample with n=800 (2), and the sample with n=1000 (1) would have the smallest margin of error.

  • Margin of error is simply the “radius” (or half the width) of a confidence interval
  • Margin of error = Critical value × Standard error
  • Standard error is inversely related to sample size (SEmean = SD/√Sample size)

questions.stem: During an autopsy conducted by a forensic expert at a medical college, skeletal remains are examined. A notable feature observed is the preauricular sulcus on the ilium. The forensic expert evaluates this marker to help determine certain characteristics of the individual. What does the preauricular sulcus primarily help to determine in forensic analysis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Sex

 

  • The preauricular sulcus has been described as a characteristic of the female pelvis. The pelvic portion of the anterior sacroiliac ligament is attached to it.
  • Its prominence results from obstetrical trauma during the course of delivery which allows for differentiation between nulliparous women and males vs females who have given birth

 

 

  • Other methods used for Sex determinations are - 
    • Physical morphology: by External examination 
    • Nuclear sexing or sex chromatin or microscopic test: through examination of Buccal epithelial cells or hair follicle cells to detect the presence of ‘Barr body’.
    • Gonadal biopsy: Detection of ‘internal gonads and sex chromosomes’ (genotype sex), 
    • Gene-based test: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is used to detect SRY gene (sex-determining region of the Y-chromosome) and/or the DYZ1 region of Y chromosome which is diagnostic. 
  • Assay of testosterone levels also helps in differentiating the sex of an individual. For females, they should have levels < 10 nmol/l (lower than the lower limit of normal for male).

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Race: The preauricular sulcus does not provide reliable information regarding the race of an individual.

 

Option C. Stature: The presence or characteristics of the preauricular sulcus do not relate to the stature of an individual.

 

Option D. Age: This feature does not vary significantly with age once adulthood is reached and thus does not serve as a reliable marker for aging.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Preauricular sulcus is used for the determination of sex, one of the feature to differentiate male and female pelvis.

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: In the Kaplan-Meier method, the survival probability is recalculated at each time point where an event occurs, and it does not start a new interval with each event.

options.label: C
options.text: The Kaplan-Meier method is typically recommended for large epidemiological studies due to its need for large data sets.

options.label: D
options.text: The Kaplan-Meier method does not use predetermined intervals; it calculates survival probabilities at the exact times events occur, with each event initiating a new interval.

questions.answerText: The Kaplan-Meier method does not use predetermined intervals; it calculates survival probabilities at the exact times events occur, with each event initiating a new interval.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) The Kaplan-Meier method does not use predetermined intervals; it calculates survival probabilities at the exact times events occur, with each event initiating a new interval.

 

  • The Kaplan-Meier method is particularly useful for studies where detailed event timing is crucial.
  • It allows for the estimation of survival probabilities without the constraints of fixed intervals, making it ideal for clinical research where patient outcomes, such as those in cancer treatment studies, may not follow a uniform time pattern.
  • This method accounts for the exact time of each event (e.g., death, relapse) by recalculating the survival probability at each event time and beginning a new interval immediately following each event.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. The Kaplan-Meier method requires the use of predetermined intervals such as monthly or yearly checkpoints to assess survival rates: This is incorrect as Kaplan-Meier specifically avoids predetermined intervals.

 

Option B. In the Kaplan-Meier method, the survival probability is recalculated at each time point where an event occurs, and it does not start a new interval with each event: This is incorrect; a new interval begins with each event.

 

Option C. The Kaplan-Meier method is typically recommended for large epidemiological studies due to its need for large data sets. This is misleading; while the method can be used in large studies, it is not limited to them and is particularly valued for its flexibility and precision in smaller studies or those with detailed timing data.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Kaplan Meier Method:
  1. Is an approach for Life table analysis
  2. In KM method, ‘predetermined intervals (1 month, 1 year, etc.) are not used’
  3. Exact point in time where death took place is identified; each death terminates previous interval and a new interval is started
  4. KM method is suited for small studies

questions.stem: Identify which of the following statements is true about central tendency:

options.label: B
options.text: Median is affected by extremes of data

options.label: D
options.text: Arithmetic mean is not affected by extreme values

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Mode is qualitative

 

  • The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set and can be used for both qualitative (categorical) and quantitative (numerical) data.
  • It is particularly useful in qualitative data because it represents the most common category or attribute.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Median is qualitative: The median is a quantitative measure that represents the middle value in a data set when the values are arranged in ascending or descending order. It can be used for ordinal, interval, and ratio data, but not for nominal (purely qualitative) data.

 

Option B. Median is affected by extremes of data: This statement is false. The median is not affected by extremes (outliers) because it solely depends on the middle value(s) of the ordered data set.

 

Option D. Arithmetic mean is not affected by extreme values: This statement is false. The arithmetic mean can be greatly affected by extreme values (outliers) in the data set because it is calculated by summing all values and dividing by the number of values.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Mean and Median are determined only for quantitative data
  • Mode can be determined for both quantitative as well as qualitative data
  • Mean is affected by outliers (extreme values)
  • Median and mode are generally not affected by outliers

  • This anatomical relationship is critical for ENT specialists to understand when evaluating patients with nasolacrimal duct obstructions or other pathologies of the anterior medial inferotemporal region.

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old patient presents with hearing loss and occasional ear discharge. Otoscopic examination shows retraction of the pars flaccida of the tympanic membrane. Based on the staging of the retraction of pars flaccida shown in the image, what is the likely stage of this patient if the examination reveals a deep retraction pocket with adherent malleus, but without ossicular erosion?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Type III

 

  • The stages of pars flaccida retraction are classified based on the extent of retraction and involvement of ossicular chain:
  • Type 0 (Normal): The pars flaccida is not retracted and appears normal.
  • Type I: There is a slight retraction of the pars flaccida without touching the ossicles.
  • Type II: The retraction pocket touches the neck of the malleus but does not affect other ossicles or their function.
  • Type III: The retraction pocket is deeper, involves adhesion of the pars flaccida to the malleus, potentially leading to malleus fixation, but without erosion of the ossicles.
  • Type IV: The retraction is severe with erosion of the ossicular chain, which may lead to more significant hearing loss and other complications.
  • In the scenario described, since the retraction pocket is deep and the malleus is adherent but not eroded, it corresponds to Type III.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Identify Type III pars flaccida retraction as characterized by a deep retraction pocket with malleus adhesion but no ossicular erosion.

questions.stem: Two social workers are evaluating the needs of families for a community support program in a suburban area. They assessed 60 families to decide if they require additional social services. The results are as follows: Both social workers agreed that 22 families require additional services. Both agreed that 28 families do not require additional services. Social worker A assessed that 35 families require services and 25 do not. Social worker B assessed that 40 families require services and 20 do not. Calculate the Kappa statistic to determine the level of agreement between the two social workers regarding the need for additional services for these families.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) 0.66

 

To solve this:

 

1. Observed Agreement (Po):

 

Total agreements = Agreed 'Yes' + Agreed 'No' = 22 (Yes) + 28 (No) = 50 agreements

 𝑃𝑜=50/60 = 0.833

 

2. Expected Agreement (Pe):

  • Probability A says Yes = 35/60
  • Probability A says No = 25/60
  • Probability B says Yes = 40/60
  • Probability B says No = 20/60

 

Expected probability both say Yes = Probability A says Yes * Probability B says Yes

 

Expected probability both say No = Probability A says No * Probability B says No

 

 

Pe = (0.58 x 0.66) + (0.42 x 0.33) = 0.52

 

3. Kappa (κ) calculation:

 

 

Kappa (κ) = (0.83 – 0.52)/ (1- 0.52) = 0.66

 

Thus, the Kappa statistic is about 0.65, indicating substantial agreement between the two social workers beyond what would be expected by chance alone.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Kappa Interpretation:
    • 0 = agreement equivalent to chance.
    • 0 – 0.20 = slight agreement.
    • 0.21 – 0.40 = fair agreement.
    • 0.41 – 0.60 = moderate agreement.
    • 0.61 – 0.80 = substantial agreement.
    • 0.81 – 0.99 = near perfect agreement
    • 1 = perfect agreement.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child presents with suspected hearing loss. The otolaryngologist wants to conduct objective tests to evaluate the child's hearing ability. Which of the following tests are considered objective methods for assessing hearing? Brainstem-evoked response audiometry (BERA) Otoacoustic emissions (OAE) Pure tone audiometry Tympanometry
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) 1, 2, and 4

 

Objective hearing tests do not rely on the patient's subjective responses and can provide accurate assessments, especially in young children or patients who may not reliably respond to subjective tests like pure tone audiometry.

 

The objective tests include:

 

  • Brainstem-evoked response audiometry (BERA): This test measures electrical activity in the brainstem in response to sound stimuli. It is particularly useful in diagnosing hearing loss in infants and young children, as it does not require active participation from the patient.
  • Otoacoustic emissions (OAE): This test measures sounds that are generated by the inner ear (cochlea) in response to an auditory stimulus. The presence or absence of these emissions can help assess cochlear function, making it useful for newborn hearing screenings.
  • Tympanometry: This test measures the movement of the tympanic membrane (eardrum) in response to changes in air pressure in the ear canal. It helps evaluate middle ear function and detect conditions such as middle ear effusion or eustachian tube dysfunction.

 

Pure tone audiometry is a subjective test, as it requires the patient's active response to hearing different tones at varying frequencies and intensities, and thus is not considered an objective measure.

 

Other Options:

 

3: Incorrect, as pure tone audiometry is not an objective test.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Objective hearing tests such as BERA, OAE, and tympanometry are essential tools for diagnosing hearing loss in children, especially when patient cooperation may be limited.
  • These tests provide reliable information about the auditory pathway and middle ear function without requiring subjective feedback from the patient.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old forensic expert is called to investigate the suspicious death of a newborn found in a remote area near a community health center. The body is partially decomposed, and the primary concern is to determine whether the newborn had been alive at birth. The forensic expert decides to use several tests that are historically known to help distinguish live birth from stillbirth. Which of the following tests is not used to determine live birth?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Gettler’s test

 

Gettler's test is historically used to determine the level of chloride concentration in the heart blood to distinguish between freshwater and saltwater drowning, not to assess whether a birth was live. This test does not help in determining live birth and is therefore not relevant in scenarios where the determination of live versus stillbirth is necessary.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Ploucquet’s Test: This test is used to determine live birth by checking whether the lungs of the deceased infant float in water, suggesting the infant breathed air (i.e., was born alive).

 

Option B. Fodere’s Test: Similar to Ploucquet’s, this test also examines lung flotation but includes additional examination of lung tissue under a microscope to confirm air inhalation.

 

Option D. Wreden’s test: This test involves examining the middle ear to determine live birth. During fetal life, the middle ear contains gelatinous embryonic connective tissue, which disappears and is replaced by air after live birth. If air is found in the middle ear, it supports the idea that the newborn was alive and had taken a breath.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Tests like Ploucquet’s, Fodere’s, and Wreden’s are commonly used to assess whether a newborn was alive at birth by evaluating the lungs or middle ear. Gettler’s test, used to determine drowning, is not relevant in assessing live birth.

questions.stem: In India, the dengue virus persists during inter-epidemic periods through a direct man-mosquito-man transmission cycle. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the virus's survival during these periods of low human infection?

options.label: B
options.text: Dormant or latent phase in human hosts

options.label: C
options.text: Transovarian transmission of the virus in mosquitoes

questions.answerText: Transovarian transmission of the virus in mosquitoes
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Transovarian transmission of the virus in mosquitoes

 

  • Transovarian transmission is a mechanism through which the dengue virus is passed from an infected female mosquito to its offspring through its eggs.
  • This allows the virus to persist in mosquito populations even during periods when there is a reduction in human cases.
  • This method of survival helps maintain the presence of the virus in regions like India during the inter-epidemic periods, ensuring that the virus can re-emerge when conditions are favorable for another outbreak.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Presence of a non-human reservoir: Incorrect. Unlike some other arboviruses, the dengue virus does not rely on non-human animal reservoirs for its survival. The primary vector is the Aedes mosquito, and the cycle is primarily between humans and mosquitoes.

 

Option B. Dormant or latent phase in human hosts: Incorrect. The dengue virus does not establish a latent phase in humans. Once infected, humans can carry the virus for a limited period during the acute phase of the illness, but they are not long-term carriers of the virus.

 

Option D. Poor community sanitation and hygiene: Incorrect. While poor sanitation can contribute to increased breeding sites for mosquitoes and higher transmission rates, it does not explain how the virus survives during periods when human infection rates are low. The transovarian transmission in mosquitoes is the key factor in virus persistence.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • The dengue virus survives during the inter-epidemic periods through transovarian transmission within mosquito populations, where infected female Aedes mosquitoes pass the virus to their offspring.
  • This ensures the persistence of the virus even when human infection rates are low.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy

 

  • Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) is an inherited mitochondrial condition that generally presents in young males as painless, progressive vision loss, typically beginning in one eye and soon affecting the other.
  • Key features include optic disc hyperemia, edema, circumpapillary telangiectasia, and a centrocecal scotoma on perimetry, while pupillary responses remain intact.

Option B. Acute Papilledema: Characterized by bilateral optic disc swelling due to raised intracranial pressure, but it generally does not present with sequential monocular vision loss or centrocecal scotoma.
 

Option C. Toxic optic neuropathy: Presents with bilateral, symmetric visual loss, typically associated with toxic exposure. However, this patient shows sequential vision loss in both eyes, which is more characteristic of LHON.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) is characterized by painless, sequential vision loss, typically beginning in young males.

  • c. Adipocere (c2): Adipocere, or "grave wax," is formed by the transformation of body fat into a waxy substance, typically seen in bodies exposed to a moist environment. This is well-depicted in Image 2.

 

Educational Objective:
 

Suggillation involves discoloration due to blood pooling, putrefaction is the decomposition of tissues due to bacterial activity, and adipocere results from chemical changes in fatty tissues, often under moist conditions.

questions.stemHtml: A researcher is analyzing the relationship between the dosage of a new drug (variable X) and the reduction in blood pressure (variable Y) in a group of hypertensive patients. The scatter plot below displays the data collected from this study. Based on the plot, what conclusion can be drawn about the relationship between the drug dosage and blood pressure reduction?

options.label: A
options.text: There is a strong positive correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction.

options.label: B
options.text: There is a negative correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction.

options.label: C
options.text: The data shows no significant correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction.

options.label: D
options.text: The relationship between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction is non-linear.

questions.answerText: There is a strong positive correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) There is a strong positive correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction.

 

  • The scatter plot shows that as X (drug dosage) increases, Y (blood pressure reduction) also increases, which is characteristic of a positive correlation.
  • The data points tend to form an upward trend, indicating that higher doses of the drug are associated with greater reductions in blood pressure.
  • This type of relationship is often seen when increasing a medication dose results in a stronger therapeutic effect.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. There is a negative correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction: Incorrect. A negative correlation would indicate that as the drug dosage increases, the reduction in blood pressure decreases. The plot shows the opposite trend, with both increasing together.

 

Option C. The data shows no significant correlation between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction: Incorrect. The scatter plot clearly shows a pattern where higher X values (dosage) are associated with higher Y values (reduction), indicating a significant positive correlation.

 

Option D. The relationship between drug dosage and blood pressure reduction is non-linear: Incorrect. The scatter plot suggests a linear trend, where changes in X correspond consistently with changes in Y, forming an approximately straight-line pattern.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Scatter plots are valuable for visualizing relationships between two continuous variables.

questions.stemHtml: A 58-year-old diabetic male presents with progressive worsening of vision. On examination, fundus findings suggest neovascularization. Fluorescein angiography findings is shown in the image. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Proliferative diabetic retinopathy

 

  • The image demonstrates the features of proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), characterized by neovascularization arising from the optic nerve head (neovascularization of the disc, NVD), as well as neovascularization along larger retinal vessels and elsewhere (NVE).
  • These new, fragile blood vessels develop in response to retinal ischemia and can lead to severe complications like vitreous hemorrhage or retinal detachment if untreated.
  • The presence of neovascularization is a key distinguishing feature of PDR.

 

Other Options:
 

Option A. Mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR): In mild NPDR, microaneurysms and intraretinal hemorrhages are present, but there is no neovascularization, which is the hallmark of proliferative disease.
 

Option B. Severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy: Severe NPDR is characterized by increased microaneurysms, venous beading, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA) but still lacks the neovascularization seen in PDR.
 

Option C. Birdshot choroidopathy: Birdshot choroidopathy presents with characteristic yellow-white lesions scattered across the fundus and is not typically associated with neovascularization. It is a type of posterior uveitis that affects the choroid and retina bilaterally.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Proliferative diabetic retinopathy is the advanced stage of diabetic eye disease, marked by neovascularization, which requires aggressive treatment like laser photocoagulation to prevent severe visual loss.
  • It is crucial for diabetics, particularly those with a long history or poorly controlled diabetes, to undergo regular eye examinations for early detection and management of diabetic retinopathy.

questions.stemHtml: A 40-year-old man presents to the emergency department with pain and swelling in his left ear, which developed over the past 2 days. He mentions a history of repeated trauma to the ear from his job as a boxing coach. On physical examination, the left ear shows erythema, tenderness, and a swollen, indurated pinna with no visible discharge. The tympanic membrane appears normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Perichondritis

 

  • The clinical presentation of painful, erythematous swelling over the auricle in a patient with a history of trauma suggests perichondritis.
  • Perichondritis is an infection of the perichondrium, typically occurring after trauma, lacerations, or surgical incisions to the ear.
  • The most common causative organism is Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
  • If left untreated, it can lead to cartilage necrosis, resulting in a "cauliflower ear" deformity, which is often seen in individuals exposed to repeated ear trauma, such as boxers and wrestlers.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Otitis externa: Otitis externa typically presents with pain, itching, and discharge from the ear canal, but it does not involve the pinna itself.

 

Option C. Chondrodermatitis helicis: Chondrodermatitis helicis presents as a painful nodule on the helix or antihelix, caused by chronic pressure and not by infection.

 

Option D. Auricular cellulitis: Auricular cellulitis can present with erythema and swelling, but it involves the soft tissue of the auricle and not specifically the cartilage, and it is not associated with a history of trauma as prominently.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Perichondritis of the ear commonly results from trauma or surgery and can progress to cartilage necrosis if untreated.
  • It typically requires antibiotic therapy targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa and may present as a painful, erythematous swelling of the auricle without tympanic membrane involvement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an indication of high tracheostomy? (NEET PG 2018)

options.label: D
options.text: Suspicion of Laryngeal carcinoma planned for surgery later

questions.answerText: Suspicion of Laryngeal carcinoma planned for surgery later
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Suspicion of Laryngeal carcinoma planned for surgery later

 

A high tracheostomy is done above the level of thyroid isthmus (isthmus lies against II, III and IV tracheal rings). It violates the first ring of trachea. Tracheostomy at this site can cause perichondritis of the cricoid cartilage and subglottic stenosis and is always avoided.

 

Only indication for high tracheostomy is carcinoma of the larynx because in such cases, the total larynx anyway would ultimately be removed and a fresh tracheostome made in a clean area lower down.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Vocal cord palsy - Not an indication for high tracheostomy as it does not necessitate altering the anatomy at the level of the isthmus or above.

 

Option B. Tracheomalacia - This condition, characterized by a weakness of the tracheal support cartilage, does not require a high tracheostomy. Treatment usually involves support lower in the trachea.

 

Option C. Foreign body obstruction - Removal of a foreign body typically does not require a high tracheostomy. This procedure would be too high to effectively clear an obstruction that is likely situated lower in the airway.

 

Educational Objective:

 

High tracheostomy is specifically indicated for suspicion of laryngeal carcinoma planned for surgery, as this condition requires eventual removal of the larynx, allowing for the creation of a fresh tracheostome in a new, clean area.

questions.stem: Where is the electrode placed in cochlear implant procedures? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Scala tympani

 

The electrode of a cochlear implant is placed in the Scala tympani.

 

A cochlear implant works by producing meaningful electrical stimulation of the auditory nerve where degeneration of the hair cells in the cochlea has progressed to a point such that amplification provided by hearing aids is no longer effective.

 

The principle of cochlear implant surgery is to place the electrode array within the scala tympani of the cochlea. This allows the electrodes to be in close proximity to the spiral ganglion cells and their dendrites (that lie in the modiolus and osseous spiral lamina of the cochlea, respectively).

 

There are broadly two surgical techniques to approach the cochlea for implantation:

 

  1. The facial recess approach where a simple cortical mastoidectomy is done. The facial recess is opened by performing a posterior tympanotomy. The stapes, promontory and round window niche are identified. Cochleostomy is then performed anteroinferior to the round window membrane to a diameter of 1.0 - 1.6 mm depending on the electrode to be used.
  2. The pericanal techniques where a tympanomeatal flap is elevated to perform a cochleostomy either by endaural or postaural approach. In the pericanal techniques a bony tunnel is drilled along the external canal towards the middle ear. The examples of pericanal techniques include the Veria and suprameatal recess approach.

 

The following criteria help define candidacy for cochlear implantation:

 

  1. Bilateral severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss.
  2. Little or no benefit from hearing aids.
  3. No medical contraindication for surgery.
  4. Realistic expectation.
  5. Good family and social support toward habilitation.
  6. Adequate cognitive function to be able to use the device.

 

 

Other Options:
 

Option A. Round window - Not typically the site for electrode placement in cochlear implants.

 

Option B. Oval window - Also not used for electrode placement; this structure connects the middle ear to the inner ear.

 

Option C. Scala vestibuli - Another perilymph-filled cavity in the cochlea, but not the preferred location for electrode placement due to its anatomy and relation to the auditory pathways.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The scala tympani is the preferred site for electrode placement in cochlear implant surgery to ensure optimal auditory nerve stimulation, highlighting the importance of precision in surgical approaches to maximize the benefits of the implant.

questions.stem: Which organ is the earliest to undergo putrefaction from the given options? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Brain

 

Among the given options, the brain is the first organ to undergo putrefaction. The process of putrefaction involves the decomposition of body tissues and follows a specific order from early to late stages.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Heart: The heart putrefies after the brain but before the kidneys.

 

Option C. Kidney: The kidneys putrefy after the heart.

 

Option D. Prostate: The prostate putrefies very late in the process, even after the kidneys.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The order of organ putrefaction (early to late) is as follows:

 

  1. Larynx and trachea
  2. Liver and lungs
  3. Brain
  4. Heart
  5. Kidney
  6. Prostate and Non Gravid uterus
  7. Skin, muscle, tendons
  8. Bones and teeth

 

Prostate and Non gravid uterus are organs which putrefy very late. The gravid uterus putrefies earlier.

 

Mnemonic: LBHK

 

L for larynx, liver, lungs, B for brain H for Heart, K for Kidney

questions.stem: Which of the following would be prescribed for simple myopic astigmatism? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. -1.00 DC X 180 degree

 

  • The correct prescription for simple myopic astigmatism is -1.00 DC × 180 degrees.
  • Simple myopic astigmatism means that one principal meridian of the eye is in focus on the retina, while the other principal meridian is in front of the retina.
  • There are three components to the prescription of glasses for astigmatism: 
    1. The power of the spherical component (convex or concave dioptre sphere),
    2. The power of the cylinder (convex or concave dioptre cylinder),
    3. The axis (orientation) of the cylinder.

 

For example: -1.00 DC × 180 degree

 

This prescription indicates that the individual has simple astigmatism, which means one meridian of the eye is in focus while the other is not. In this case, the unfocused meridian is myopic (nearsighted) and requires correction with a concave cylinder lens. The strength of the cylinder lens is -1.00 diopters (DC). The axis of the cylinder is oriented at 180 degrees, which represents the meridian that is most affected by astigmatism.

 

Types of astigmatism:

 

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. +1.00 DS: This represents a convex spherical lens for hypermetropia (farsightedness) and is not used for astigmatism correction.

 

Option C. -1.00 DS: This represents a concave spherical lens for simple myopia (nearsightedness) but does not correct astigmatism.

 

Option D. -1.00 DS -1.00 DC X 180 degree: This represents a prescription for compound myopic astigmatism, where both meridians are myopic, one corrected by the spherical component and the other by the cylindrical component.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Simple myopic astigmatism requires correction with a cylindrical lens that corrects the myopic meridian, typically specified with the cylinder power and the axis. The correct prescription for simple myopic astigmatism in this case is -1.00 DC X 180 degrees.

questions.stem: The only extraocular muscle with sympathetic nerve supply is?
questions.solutionHtml:
the Sympathetic chain of head and neck leads to HORNER’S SYNDROME characterised by a triad of ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis.

 

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Superior Rectus: This muscle, responsible for elevating the eye, is innervated by the oculomotor nerve (Cranial Nerve III), not by sympathetic nerves.

 

Option B. Levator Palpebrae Superioris (LPS): The LPS raises the upper eyelid and is also innervated by the oculomotor nerve. It is not supplied by sympathetic nerves.

 

Optiion C. Medial Rectus: This muscle, which moves the eye medially (towards the nose), is innervated by the oculomotor nerve as well. It does not receive sympathetic innervation.

 

Educational Objective:

 

The only extraocular muscle with sympathetic nerve supply is Müller’s Muscle, a smooth muscle in the upper eyelid that aids in eyelid elevation.
